description: We are three university students from Athens, passionate about astrophysics, planetary and geospatial sciences, and remote sensing: a geologist and natural hazards researcher, MSc student in GIS (NKUA); a first-year geology student (NKUA) interested in GIS; and a final-year mining and metallurgical engineering student (NTUA) interested in mineralogy and GIS. The name of our team honours Lynkeus, the sharp-eyed Argonaut lookout, and our team image is Hevelius's constellation Lynx.
summary: Lynkeus is an open-source web GIS platform for the analysis of surface change from NISAR radar data. A user finds the NISAR products of any area and period in NASA's catalogue, obtains the layers needed, cut to the area of interest by NASA Harmony, and views them on a map in the browser. The platform then maps radar backscatter, interferometric coherence, line-of-sight surface displacement and soil moisture, computes the change between two dates, and plots time series at a point or over the area. The backscatter and time-series computations follow the NISAR notebooks of the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF NISAR Cookbook). On NISAR products of a test area, Lynkeus reproduces the results of these notebooks, of GDAL and of MintPy exactly, or to within 0.000003 dB in the time series.
details:
Lynkeus is a web GIS platform that works directly on the data services of NASA. The user searches NASA's Common Metadata Repository (CMR) for NISAR products by product type, validation level, area, period, orbit and polarisation, or by product name, and the products found are listed and drawn as footprints on the map. The user signs in with a token of their own Earthdata Login account; the server verifies the token with the public keys of Earthdata Login and keeps it in memory only. For each requested layer, NASA Harmony cuts the product to the area of interest, and Lynkeus stores the result as a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF with a STAC metadata record. The browser reads this file directly and draws it with OpenLayers, so the colour scale and the value range can be changed without any computation on the server.

The analysis consists of twelve tools, grouped by the quantity that NISAR measures: radar backscatter (map of one date, change between two dates, time series, thematic map of classes), interferometric coherence (map of one pair of dates, change between two pairs, time series), line-of-sight surface displacement (one pair, time series) and soil moisture (map of one date, change between two dates, time series). A time series is computed at a point or as one value for the whole area. In addition, the platform writes the citation of the NASA datasets behind each layer, with their DOIs. A user can also connect a personal computer through the program Lynkeus Server (release v0.1.0); that computer then runs the user's jobs and stores the resulting layers.

On NISAR products of a test area, the lower Merrimack River, Massachusetts, USA, Lynkeus reproduces the results of existing open-source software. The backscatter map and the backscatter change are identical, in every cell, to the results of the ASF NISAR Cookbook notebooks. The time series of backscatter and of coherence differ from those of the Cookbook by at most 2.1 × 10⁻⁶ dB and 1.2 × 10⁻⁸, respectively. The coherence change and the soil-moisture change are identical, in every cell, to the results of gdal raster calc (GDAL 3.12.2), and the line-of-sight displacement is identical to the result of MintPy 1.6.4 for two interferometric pairs. The coherence of one pair and the soil moisture of one date show the layer of the product without modification, and were therefore checked against the product files.

Of the types of surface change that the challenge names, the present tools apply to wetlands and floodplains, deforestation and wildfire, crops, soil moisture, and deformation from earthquakes and coastal subsidence. Glaciers and sea ice are not yet covered, because their motion is measured with pixel offsets: Lynkeus retrieves the pixel-offset product (GOFF) but has no tool for it. Two further limits apply: a time series is shown as a chart and not as an animated map, and the displacement is not corrected for atmospheric effects.

The server is written in Python (FastAPI, earthaccess, harmony-py, Rasterio, NumPy) and the interface in TypeScript (React, OpenLayers). On every pull request, automated checks on GitHub test the formatting, the types and the functions of the code. The source code is public under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3, and a public team log records each decision of the team with its reason.

Source code: https://github.com/AlexandrosLiaskos/lynkeus.
Team log: https://lynkeus.nkua.cloud/team-log/.
